main_dirt.bias_notes: Main 1-mile dirt oval with a fair 1,010-foot home straight. Early speed ('E') and tactical pressers ('P') hold a distinct advantage, particularly in two-turn routes where clearing early avoids wide-trip penalties on the broad turns. Deep closers require an unsustainable front-end speed duel to win.
main_dirt.post_bias: In dirt sprints (5.5f and 6f), middle barriers (stalls 3-6) are preferred. In two-turn routes (1m to 1m70y), inside barriers (stalls 1-4) hold a significant advantage before the short run-up to the first turn.

franks_turf.bias_notes: Tight inner turf circuit with a short 940-foot straightaway. Heavily favors tactical speed horses who can secure a ground-saving spot along the rail before the second turn. Downgrade deep closers unless a blistering early pace is guaranteed.
franks_turf.post_bias: Inside barriers (stalls 1-4) hold a distinct edge due to the short distance between starting gates and tight inner bends.

handicapping_angles.dirt_route_speed_bias: In 1-mile and 1m70y dirt route races, prioritize front-runners ('E') and pressers ('EP') capable of establishing early position before the first turn.
handicapping_angles.turf_inside_rail_advantage: On Frank's Turf Course, target runners drawn in Stalls 1 through 4 with tactical early pace. Wide runners frequently get forced 3-wide around the tight bends.
handicapping_angles.fair_grounds_and_oaklawn_shippers: Heavily upgrade class-dropping shippers arriving from major circuits like Fair Grounds or Oaklawn Park into local Louisiana Downs claiming/allowance ranks.
handicapping_angles.summer_heat_and_fast_track: During peak summer months, dry dirt plays fast and favors on-pace runners. On wet/sealed tracks, the inside rail often becomes a lightning-fast speed strip.
